sonnet.q1: The old engine charges and writes the ledger. The new engine's output goes only to the shadow store (never charged, not in the ledger).
sonnet.q2: The new engine charges and writes the ledger. The old engine computes every invoice into the shadow store and never charges.
sonnet.q3: 7 days in a row with a mismatch rate under 0.1%, and at least 5,000 invoices compared. A person makes the move (sets the flag).
sonnet.q4: The billing monitor, automatically, when the new engine's charge failure rate is above 2% over any 10-minute window. Only in both or new_only (shadow errors are only recorded).
sonnet.q5: Every rollback ends in old_only. Before the new engine can take over again, the rollout must go through shadow again, and its 7-day count starts over (gates reset).
sonnet.q6: From day 35 in new_only (after 35 days without a rollback); from then on there is no way back because the old engine is decommissioned. The document does not give a further reason (usage event log is kept 35 days, but the document doesn't explicitly link them).
sonnet.q8: The nightly comparison job writes results to comparison_results. Evidence location beyond that, and any enforcement mechanism preventing early promotion, is NOT STATED; the document only says a person makes each move and gives the gate requirements.
sonnet.q9: The billing monitor. It measures the new engine's charge failure rate (over any 10-minute window). When it is above 2% in both or new_only, it automatically starts a rollback.
sonnet.q10: NOT STATED. The document only says charging is paused first so nobody is charged during the switch, and resumed at the last step; it does not say how due charges are handled or when they are made (reconcile ensures no due charge is dropped).
sonnet.q11: The reconcile step, done by customer and billing period, ensures no one is charged twice. Repeating a step must also not charge twice. How reconcile does this is NOT STATED.
sonnet.q12: Charging stays paused (resumed only at the final step); the document does not otherwise describe the billing state. The failed step is run again, using the rollback record to resume from the last finished step. If reconcile finds a conflict, charging is not resumed and on-call is alerted. Who is paged for a repeatedly failing step is an open question.
